/sig network
If you have specific scenarios where MD5's use has caused issues like (integration failures, and compliance errors), sharing those examples would help prioritize and shape the implementation.

I will raise PR if it's triaged.
/assign

Can we first explain in the issue what is the proposal?

There is a long discussion about FIPS complain here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129075 and it seems better to tackle all these related issues in a single theme instead of individual PRs

I think we can change the MD5 to pretty much any other hash function.  It's not security-sensitive, but ACK that FIPS just blanket disallows MD5.

The only risk I see here is that a different hash MIGHT change the results order, but it's been a LONG time since I looked at that code.

If someone were to send a PR and proof that it doesn't break anyone (i.e. it won't cause instant churn when the cluster is upgraded, which I am pretty sure it won't) I would be happy to consider it.  Since it is not security, the lightest weight hash we can find would be best.

I don't really want to change that code any more than needed, so while there may be better ways to do it, small delta is best :)

This might be the first one that errors on building, but it's not the only md5 usage in the project.

https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Akubernetes%2Fkubernetes%20md5.New()&type=code
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Akubernetes%2Fkubernetes%20crypto%2Fmd5&type=code

I busy with some other work unassigning my self
/unassign

Note that there are currently at least 6 places using md5, presumably removing only one is of limited utility. It seems like we'd need to remove all of them AND ensure that no new usage is added.

We have tooling to mark "unwanted imports".

> I think we can change the MD5 to pretty much any other hash function. It's not security-sensitive, but ACK that FIPS just blanket disallows MD5.
> 
> The only risk I see here is that a different hash MIGHT change the results order, but it's been a LONG time since I looked at that code.
> 
> If someone were to send a PR and proof that it doesn't break anyone (i.e. it won't cause instant churn when the cluster is upgraded, which I am pretty sure it won't) I would be happy to consider it. Since it is not security, the lightest weight hash we can find would be best.
> 
> I don't really want to change that code any more than needed, so while there may be better ways to do it, small delta is best :)

@thockin if one were to work on this, what sort of test would constitute proof that it doesn't break anything?

For the specific case of Endpoints - I would craft an `Endpoints` YAML which is ill-formed on input (which will trigger the `RepackSubsets` logic), create an instance of it, and record the resulting object in the API.  Do this with md5 (as is) and with your replacement and compare the resulting objects.

I am new here, trying to work on this issue :)

> Note that there are currently at least 6 places using md5, presumably removing only one is of limited utility. It seems like we'd need to remove all of them AND ensure that no new usage is added.
> 
> We have tooling to mark "unwanted imports".

@BenTheElder  Here we are using standard crypto/md5 library and do not think it is possible to mark as unwanted in `unwanted-dependencies.json` as the tooling is based on the output of `go mod graph` that do not show standard libraries.
Could probably switch tooling to build around `go list -json <path>/...`

> I think we can change the MD5 to pretty much any other hash function.

Probably. It may be somewhat disruptive to performance and or caching depending on the algorithm and usage. md5 is cheap.

>  It's not security-sensitive, but ACK that FIPS just blanket disallows MD5.

I think it's not that simple and ultimately it's up to the distributor to certify their usage, libraries, etc.

https://crypto.stackexchange.com/a/92075

The new go FIPS crypto stuff has a "strict" (now called "only") mode that may make it easier to certify by just disallowing any non-allowed algorithms from the stdlib, but there are cases where an algorithm that wouldn't be allowed for something security sensitive may be allowed.

**further** that mode is not alone sufficient to certify compliance: https://go.dev/doc/security/fips140

> When GODEBUG=fips140=only is used, in addition to the above, cryptographic algorithms that are not FIPS 140-3 compliant will return an error or panic. Note that this mode is a best effort and can’t guarantee compliance with all FIPS 140-3 requirements.

> @BenTheElder Here we are using standard crypto/md5 library and do not think it is possible to mark as unwanted in unwanted-dependencies.json as the tooling is based on the output of go mod graph that do not show standard libraries.

Good point. This might not be the right tool for the job.

In the meantime, @harzallah, want to take a look at the endpoints issue outlined above? https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129652#issuecomment-2596398148 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129652#issuecomment-3145345159

-----

For other usage aside from endpoints ....

I'm not sure if changing the pod UID bit would be non-disruptive ...?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/81affffa1b8d8079836f4cac713ea8d1b2bbf10f/pkg/kubelet/config/common.go#L60-L74

cc @tallclair 

~Anything should be fine for the kubeadm usage,

Instead of rewriting unwanted-dependencies, we can use `forbidigo` for preventing new usage: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511

While doing that, I noticed the kubeadm usage is extremely trivial and self-contained, so I migrated it.

The endpoints usage still needs working through, as do the others.

/sig architecture
/area code-organization

BTW "good first issue" is a label we use with a higher bar for documenting exactly how to get started etc:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22good%20first%20issue%22

https://www.kubernetes.dev/docs/guide/help-wanted/
https://www.kubernetes.dev/docs/guide/

I think this doesn't meet that bar, e.g.:
> If someone were to send a PR and proof that it doesn't break anyone (i.e. it won't cause instant churn when the cluster is upgraded, which I am pretty sure it won't) I would be happy to consider it. Since it is not security, the lightest weight hash we can find would be best.

May actually be a bit complex. Which is why this is "help wanted".

This could still be a first project, but it is probably best as a second project.

> I'm not sure if changing the pod UID bit would be non-disruptive ...?

The actual UID is only internal to the kubelet... mirror pods have their UID stomped by the API server. The kubelet records the calculated UID in an annotation, but that's fine to have change between minor versions (pod annotation change doesn't break or restart or do anything disruptive)

> For the specific case of Endpoints - I would craft an `Endpoints` YAML which is ill-formed on input (which will trigger the `RepackSubsets` logic), create an instance of it, and record the resulting object in the API. Do this with md5 (as is) and with your replacement and compare the resulting objects.

I was expecting a much narrower tweak to switch the hasher to something fast like fnv and prove performance is equivalent with a local unit test benchmark.

I would like to avoid forcing all Endpoints objects to be refreshed in some different order, if we can.  It seems unlikely to cause problems (it's not really clearly ordered anyway) but ...

Too paranoid for Jordan?  Maybe that's a warning sign :)
oh, I missed the hash informs the slice sorting for what gets written to the API... ick. I thought it was just used for uniquing internally.
It's been a LONG time since I dug into that code, so `<handwaving>`

`staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/util/util.go` `HashObject` doesn't appear to be used by us:
https://cs.k8s.io/?q=%5C.HashObject&i=nope&literal=nope&files=&excludeFiles=&repos=

... but it is exported

The others, aside from the kubelet change (discussed above, should be fine in a new minor version) and the endpoints bit, are pretty obviously fine to switch.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511 has preventing new usage via linter, switching the others was so trivial it didn't seem worth leaving to another PR vs adding lint-exception comments to the existing usage.

Haven't tackled endpoints yet.

> I would like to avoid forcing all Endpoints objects to be refreshed in some different order, if we can. It seems unlikely to cause problems (it's not really clearly ordered anyway) but ...

How terrible would this be on minor version upgrade? Seems like we would only shuffle them when there was an incoming update anyhow?

> How terrible would this be on minor version upgrade? Seems like we would only shuffle them when there was an incoming update anyhow?

That's what I mean, it's PROBABLY not a hug deal, I am not even 100% sure it will happen, but we should check it.

> For the specific case of Endpoints - I would craft an Endpoints YAML which is ill-formed on input (which will trigger the RepackSubsets logic), create an instance of it, and record the resulting object in the API. Do this with md5 (as is) and with your replacement and compare the resulting objects.

So ... AFAICT we only repack endpoints associated with a service / pods, we collect up the pod endpoints and then repack them here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/091f87c10bc3532041b77a783a5f832de5506dc8/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L448

We also run the repack logic in endpointslicemirroring, but that doesn't write back to the endpoints:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/091f87c10bc3532041b77a783a5f832de5506dc8/pkg/controller/endpointslicemirroring/reconciler.go#L72

I don't think there's any path where we'll just repack an endpoints object:
https://cs.k8s.io/?q=RepackSubsets&i=nope&literal=nope&files=&excludeFiles=_test.go&repos= 

So we can't super easily test Repack, but we can inspect the behavior and know that sorting at least partially by the hash will not stay identical when we change hashers.

EndpointSlice has some similar logic for comparing based on md5 hashes.

Open question remains for:
> staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/util/util.go HashObject doesn't appear to be used by us:
> https://cs.k8s.io/?q=%5C.HashObject&i=nope&literal=nope&files=&excludeFiles=&repos=
>
> ... but it is exported

This is a little difficult to search the ecosystem for even in public code, it's possible someone in the ecosystem depends on this, but it would appear in a new "minor" version anyhow.

The purpose of this utility is ambiguous and I wonder if we'd be better served by removing it?

AFAICT *none* of our subprojects are using it. The hits for `\.HashObject` in cs.k8s.io are not for that utility.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/091f87c10bc3532041b77a783a5f832de5506dc8/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/util/util.go#L44-L51

I think this is just stale code. Though again, it is public in a staging module, so it's conceivable someone depends on it.
If they do, they could copy it somewhere else, it doesn't depend on any non-public symbols and it is quite trivial.
We can definitely drop a problematic unused function from `k8s.io/kubectl`, that repo is in service of exposing the underlying logic used by kubectl commands.

Here's what I'm thinking about Endpoints/EndpointSlices, based on the code:

- ISTM that the Endpoints controller _will_ rewrite every Endpoints object the first time an fnv-using apiserver gets the lease, because the `serviceInformer` will queue a `syncService` for every Service, and `syncService` will see that the `currentEndpoints.Subsets` does not match the expected `subsets`, so it will rewrite the Endpoints.
- The EndpointSlice controller _should not_ do any new/unnecessary rewriting of EndpointSlices at any point, because it doesn't have any expected/canonical ordering of endpoints. While it does use a hash as part of reconciling the slices, the values of the hash are only used internally as a way of uniquely identifying particular ports, and don't affect what data gets written to etcd, so it doesn't matter if different instances of the controller use different hashes.
- The EndpointSliceMirroring controller _should not_ do any new rewriting, because it doesn't try to optimize its rewriting anyway; if the Endpoints object changes, then it always updates the EndpointSlice.
- The apiserver endpoint reconciler _should not_ do any new rewriting of the `kubernetes` Endpoints (EDIT: or EndpointSlice), because it doesn't require the existing Endpoints object to have the endpoints in the same order that it would have written them in.
- ~~OTOH, the apiserver endpoint reconciler _will_ rewrite the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice if the IPs aren't in `RepackSubsets` order, because that part of the reconciler just does a `DeepEqual`. This means that during an upgrade from md5-using apiservers to fnv-using apiservers, the IPs in the `kubernetes` EndpointSlice will flap back and forth between the two orders every 10 seconds until all apiservers are upgraded.~~ (EDIT: wrong, see [below](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129652#issuecomment-3228138690).)

The `kubernetes` EndpointSlice case can easily be fixed to do an order-agnostic check. Doing that for the Endpoints controller `syncService` too is obviously possible, but potentially slow for large Endpoints...

ACK @danwinship, I threw a hold on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511

> ISTM that the Endpoints controller will rewrite every Endpoints object the first time an fnv-using apiserver gets the lease, because the serviceInformer will queue a syncService for every Service, and syncService will see that the currentEndpoints.Subsets does not match the expected subsets, so it will rewrite the Endpoints.

ACK ... that's annoying, but I think we can do an order independent comparison as you mentioned.

We have to walk all of them anyhow, if we really want to optimize we can do something like retaining the map(s) from RepackSubsets to use for efficient comparison ...


> OTOH, the apiserver endpoint reconciler will rewrite the kubernetes EndpointSlice if the IPs aren't in RepackSubsets order, because that part of the reconciler just does a DeepEqual. This means that during an upgrade from md5-using apiservers to fnv-using apiservers, the IPs in the kubernetes EndpointSlice will flap back and forth between the two orders every 10 seconds until all apiservers are upgraded.

This is referring to `pkg/controller/endpointslicemirroring` ?

I will have to trace this again, looking at RepackSubsets in non-test code, I didn't see the simple deep-equal that otherwise wouldn't have triggered.

We can intentionally create a permanent state of upgrading with a kind cluster containing API servers permanently at both versions, we just need to craft some test objects known to sort differently (probably anything with a few addresses ...)

> This is referring to `pkg/controller/endpointslicemirroring` ?

No, `pkg/controlplane/reconciler/`. But having looked at it again, I see that I was wrong before: [it does call `EnsureEndpointSliceFromEndpoints` even when it doesn't update the Endpoints object](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.34.0-rc.2/pkg/controlplane/reconcilers/lease.go#L238), but it passes it the _existing_ Endpoints object in that case, so `EnsureEndpointSliceFromEndpoints` will compare the existing Endpoints against the existing EndpointSlice and see that they match, and not try to update anything.

So the remaining concern is?:
> ISTM that the Endpoints controller will rewrite every Endpoints object the first time an fnv-using apiserver gets the lease, because the serviceInformer will queue a syncService for every Service, and syncService will see that the currentEndpoints.Subsets does not match the expected subsets, so it will rewrite the Endpoints.

Which we can fix with an order-independent comparison.

A naive implementation could be to just re-pack the existing object before diffing.
An order-independent diff could be a bit cheaper, if messier, and still not free.

> A naive implementation could be to just re-pack the existing object before diffing.
> An order-independent diff could be a bit cheaper, if messier, and still not free.

Intermediate option: do the existing order-dependent diff first, and if it fails, _then_ repack the existing subsets and try the diff again.

FWIW, the existing code is not especially optimized.

Circled back to this ... 

> Intermediate option: do the existing order-dependent diff first, and if it fails, then repack the existing subsets and try the diff again.

I like this, it is trivial but ~cheap, and with endpoints being deprecated anyhow, I'm not sure it's worth trying to avoid, especially given:

> FWIW, the existing code is not especially optimized.

Testing upgrade behaviors is fairly annoying at the moment.

Added https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511/commits/f5c42c848db9d5504e61beba81d7ac0632aff82a to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511 and rebased. (And confirmed the unit test fails if I revert the controller change).

Note that Go's `fips140=only` mode is not going to work, even with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511

- Websocket sha1: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/74630#issuecomment-3222962269 (which is probably fine in practice but is blocked by `fips140=only` simply blocking the algorithm rather than a human considering the context, speak to whoever is handling certification for you)
  - Websocket cannot be dropped anytime soon AFAIK
- https://github.com/golang/go/issues/75148

Possibly more.

I still think we should retire MD5, but compliance remains a more complicated topic and `only` mode would require further work.

> Note that Go's fips140=only mode is not going to work, even with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133511

To clarify, I added a local diff to set the godebug option in the main module / workspace and attempted to bring up a cluster, which failed due to related errors. The only mode is still too strict / incompatible, see above.

title: Remove the MD5 hash function for FIPS compliance
